observation.visible_scene: A calm lake at dawn/dusk. The sky shows a pink-to-blue gradient with two long diagonal contrails. On the right is a small island silhouetted with tall conifers, mirrored in the still water. Along the left horizon a dark tree line sits against a glowing orange band, with a thin layer of mist hovering over the water. In the mid-left distance a small boat silhouette floats; near center a low floating dock/platform with a metal ladder is visible. The foreground water holds scattered lily pads, a patch of concentric ripples, and the dark silhouette of a boat's bow (and an outboard motor) at the very bottom edge.
visible_changes: The overall framing is fixed: the tree island, dock, distant boat, contrails and foreground bow hold the same positions relative to the frame edges throughout, indicating no camera pan or zoom.
The concentric ripples in the center-foreground persist and slowly evolve/shimmer across the sequence, with their ring pattern subtly shifting rather than translating.
The low mist over the left water and tree line drifts and changes shape/density only slightly over the clip.
The orange sky-glow reflection on the water surface shifts faintly as the ripples move.
The distant boat and the dock remain essentially stationary in position within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced the ripples (e.g., a fish, an object, wind) is not visible.
Whether the distant boat is actually moving over a longer time span cannot be determined from this short, near-static segment.
The cause of the mist's drift is unseen.
Events before t=0 and after t=1.35 s are outside the crop.
uncertain_details: Whether the ripples are genuinely expanding outward or merely shimmering in place is hard to confirm at this frame spacing.
The magnitude of the mist change is subtle and could partly be compression noise.
Any very small camera drift is below reliable detection; the scene appears locked-down.
